title: Brilliant app - wish I could pay a one-off fee for life.
body:
I just started using it and it’s honestly brilliant. It’s incredibly feature-rich, giving you plenty in free mode, while also offering substantial extras for premium mode. For me, the game changer is the Eisenhower Matrix. I’m really bad for doing things that aren’t a priority at the expense of other things even though I keep a bullet journal for my tasks. When my days are hectic I’m usually pretty good, but on the less hectic days, this is where I go astray. Having an editable EM is a revelation for me and elevates the app above all others, and it will work perfectly with my bullet journal.

I tried a few other big name apps, which all give free versions, but they’re so limited that they’re simply not workable in the free version. They all provide trials, like TickTick, but I uninstalled them without using the free trial. A free workable version, that still keeps some goodies for premium, and is really good will make me want to buy it, simply because it’s so good and because the developers are so generous with what they provide. However, none of them provide the EM. 

I have one single gripe and it’s a wider gripe for most services these days, but there’s no lifetime fee. I’m fed up with subscriptions because they all add up every month.  Tick Tick is actually a tiny subscription, especially compared to others, so it’s definitely worth paying for but it’d be nice to have the option to buy it outright too, offering the developer team some security as well. Otherwise, I can’t praise this app highly enough.

title: Amazing Organisational Tool
body:
This app works really well at being an excellent tool for to do lists, and organising your life! I use it as both a standard to do list, and essentially a calendar. Instead of having a calendar and having to click into every individual day to see what is planned, I use Tick Tick to schedule the days in advance and so I know even at a swift glance what I’m up to on a certain date! 

This app also works well for giving further detail to the to do list or bulleted item. You can add notes or images to the entry, which is really helpful, for example I normally add an entry when I know I am going into the city, and will then use the image note feature to save a picture of the train time table with the entry which is really useful. 

You can also make recurring events such as weekly tasks, which is a great feature, and you can tag and separate your tasks too into work, home, normal etc. I love the time and urgency feature in which you can tag how urgent it is, and what time it should alert you to the task as a notification if necessary. 

All of this is on the free version, and I find it’s very functional and the best organisational app I have found so far! It does everything that I need and all in one easy place, been using this app for over 2 years now and I’ve certainly tried, tested, and loved it!

title: Best out there
body: I never leave reviews but I just have to for this app. This is everything I was looking for! Originally, I was put off by the ‘In-App Purchases’ disclaimer as so many apps are virtually unusable without a subscription, but the features offered FOR FREE by this app are phenomenal, with no ads! And it’s so affordable if you’re willing to pay! I searched for so long for a To Do list app that was useful for deadlines and offered both an overview and a deep dive into tasks that had to be done, as well as sub-tasks,  and this is that very app. I love how customisable it is  — sort tasks into personalised lists, add tags to find them easily, rearrange the sidebar to your liking, set sub-tasks OR checklists, assign emojis and colours to your lists, put lists in folders or add sections to your lists. The app comes with sections to see what’s coming up Today, Tomorrow, in the Next 7 Days, and Later, as well as a calendar function for an overview (though the calendar somewhat lacks without the subscription), as well as a free pomodoro timer, an Eisenhower Matrix and a place to set and track habits. The widgets are a lifesaver, and customisable too, and can be changed to show anything from all of your tasks, one of your lists or today, the next 7 days or, with premium, a calendar with all your tasks blocked in. I have just subscribed to the premium version of the app after several weeks of use because the Eisenhower Matrix and calendar are really useful features that aren’t AS useful without the subscription, though still usable. Considering the low price and how brilliant this app has been, I just had to get the premium version, but believe me, it was great even without paying. Honestly, I could not ask more from an app!

title: Thought it was the best... until I reached the top 4-6%... then??? No!!!

It became totally unworkable, it was literally a case of me using the app so much to try to keep moving against what appeared to be a relentlessly defeating tide... that it really started to impinge on my workload & I had to stop. Which is a shame because until then it was the best app out there, and I have yet to find another which I am as happy to work with.
Shame guys... just as you think, after two or three years, you are about to win the grand, super achiever prizes... the earth starts slipping away like mud beneath your feet and you’re spending waaaay too much time to even stay in one place. I hope they’ve fixed that up now... but otherwise, I’m looking elsewhere.

That is syncing, specifically background sync of the iOS app not working at all. As an example, if i create a task on my Mac or Apple Watch it does not appear on the phone app until the app is actually launched and manually refreshed. 

This is frustrating if I create a task on my Apple Watch, as the phone app is just not aware of the task until I actually go into the app and force it to refresh/sync. This means in some cases the phone app will not notify me of tasks (because it doesn’t even know they exist!).

This is a massive deal breaker, I mean one of the primary functions of this app is to notify of important tasks and it can’t always do that! It’s not just me either, search online and users have reported this issue multiple times over the years. The dev responds saying they are looking to improve the background automatic syncing but it’s still a problem. I was all ready to pay for the premium upgrade but now I’m unfortunately uninstalling the app. Such a shame.

title: Best to-do app around
body:
I‘ve tried every task app around and found TickTick to be the best of the bunch.

It has all the basics like colour-coded lists, priority settings and tags, with a decent free tier unlike some other apps that make you pay just to get tags and notifications. 

Some of my favourite features are merge tasks (I use this to make my planned work tasks for the day into one checklist), saved templates and the percentage progress indicator which is automatic with subtasks but you can also drag it across manually on any task if you like.

And it has a few features that really should be standard in every task manager yet are almost always missing: calendar view, ability to view calendar events from multiple calendars, a proper notes section as well as comments, and proper subtasks in steps that don’t get added to your task count.

However the themes aren’t great - worst of all, dark mode is horrible as the text is all orange. There are lots of new colour options but loads of them look the same and frankly I preferred the old ones (I miss neon yellow). Markdown implementation is also really poor.

But it’s brilliant otherwise!

body: Excellent - I searched high and low for a good menubar to do app. I used to use Things but I've come to dislike the Projects and Areas sections  and found myself cluttering it up. I also wanted access via a menubar rather than having to open a desktop app, as it makes the whole process of writing and checking off To Dos very easy- more 'lightweight' in a good way. The category options are great, the way you can create tick-able sub-lists (or notes) inside a to-do, and rank them by priority as well as add deadlines- all brilliant. You can also log in to the online app (a substitute for a desktop app) if you need to see a full screen view or organise things more easily. Syncs perfectly with phone. Love it. Only suggested improvement is a 'search' option as sometimes I can't remember where I've put a to do item when I have several categories/lists on the go.

title: Best of the best
body:
I've tried so many task managers, literally all of them. 

All I can say is none of them offer as many polished features as ticktick. 

I can fault it. It has never crashed on me, the colour coding is beautiful, the ability to organise inside the app is unbeatable, there are smart lists, location based reminders, alarms which actually catch your attention and so many more flawless and polished features. 

Not to mention the web app, reliable syncing, and the ridiculously low price tag that comes with the pro version. 

Oh yeah, and subtasks too!! 

I used to use "Things", and got fed up with their slow progress. Fair enough, they "apparently" spend so long because they polish out all of their bugs, but I think that's a load of rubbish as Ticktick has a shed load more features and they are all flawless and perfectly functional. I genuinely don't know why ticktick isn't more popular than it is now, all I know is it should be leading the market.

So goodbye Things and hello Ticktick.

title: Best ToDo/Task Management app!!
body:
The more I use I use this app the more I value it, so I'm repeating my earlier review for the previous version - if you want to get your life & work well organized, do try it! 

This is by far the best ToDo/Task Management app I've ever used, and, believe me, I've tried hordes of them! It gives me all the features I need to organize everything I do, and it's so easy to work with that it brings a whole new level of meaning to the term user-friendly. I specially love the customizable repeats, the sub-tasks feature, which lets me track all the details I want to see while still only taking up one line on my to-do list, and today's tasks showing up in my Notifications so I can see my upcoming tasks with just one swipe. This is the Task Manager that I've been looking for - can't recommend too strongly!

title: Top To-Do List App
body: I have tried quite a few to-do list apps over the years, finding the popular ones like Wunderlist and Evernote overly complicated and others like Any.DO or RTM lacking enough detail. Over the last few months I have been using the free TickTick app and I cannot praise it enough. The app is perfectly designed for easily creating new tasks, adjusting due dates and categorizing or prioritizing tasks. I love the simplicity of the home task list screen and the amount of detail you can add within individual tasks. Other features such as the notification centre widget and reminders are also very useful. TickTick is absolutly ideal for me as a busy student and I strongly reccommend anyone giving it a go!
